l4_steps.name: Identify MRO capability gap requiring outsourcing
l4_steps.input: Maintenance program review, fleet capacity utilisation report
l4_steps.output: Outsourcing requirement specification with scope and timeline
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor qualification cycle ≤90 days from gap identification
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS capability mapping not always current; manual gap analysis against maintenance program is error-prone and reliant on engineering judgement rather than system-generated flags

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ to approved vendor shortlist via Ariba
l4_steps.input: Outsourcing requirement specification, current Approved Vendor List
l4_steps.output: RFQ package distributed to shortlisted MRO vendors
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80% of invited vendors within 14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Limited pool of EASA Part-145 / FAA-approved vendors for narrowbody heavy checks creates market concentration risk and limits competitive pricing leverage

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor Part-145 approval and capability
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (Vendor Management module)
l4_steps.input: Vendor qualification submissions, FAA/EASA Part-145 approval certificates
l4_steps.output: Approved Vendor List (AVL) update with capability ratings
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of selected vendors hold current EASA Part-145 or FAA Part-145 approval at time of contract award
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval expiry tracking in AMOS requires manual certificate uploads; no automated feed from FAA AIRS or EASA EAMR — expired approvals may go undetected until audit

l4_steps.name: Define MRO work scope and SLA requirements
l4_steps.input: Aircraft maintenance program, fleet maintenance schedule, maintenance history
l4_steps.output: Maintenance work scope document, draft SLA with TAT and quality KPIs
l4_steps.kpi: Work scope completeness score ≥95% (no unplanned post-induction scope additions attributable to pre-induction planning gaps)
l4_steps.pain_point: Scope creep during heavy checks when undocumented corrosion or structural findings emerge; AMOS work orders not pre-linked to vendor contracts, making scope-change traceability manual

l4_steps.name: Negotiate contract terms, pricing, and TAT commitments
l4_steps.input: Draft SLA, vendor commercial proposals, industry man-hour benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Signed MRO contract with TAT commitments, penalty clauses, and AWF pricing schedule
l4_steps.kpi: C-check contract TAT ≤35 days; man-hour rate within ±5% of OAG/industry benchmark
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiating fixed-price contracts with variable scope (structural findings, AD compliance work) leads to post-check cost disputes; penalty clauses rarely enforced due to vendor dependency

l4_steps.name: Load signed contract into SAP Ariba and AMOS
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba + AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Signed MRO contract, approved work scope
l4_steps.output: Active vendor contract record in both SAP Ariba and AMOS with linked work orders
l4_steps.kpi: Contract data entry accuracy 100%; dual-system load completed within 2 business days of signature
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual manual entry into SAP Ariba and AMOS creates synchronisation risk; contract amendments frequently update only one system, causing PO/work-order mismatches that surface at invoice reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Release aircraft to MRO vendor for scheduled induction
l4_steps.input: Signed maintenance work order, aircraft airworthiness release, ferry flight plan
l4_steps.output: Aircraft handover documentation, work package issued to vendor
l4_steps.kpi: On-time aircraft delivery to MRO station ≥95%; handover documentation completeness 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late aircraft delivery to MRO station (due to operational delays or AOG diversions) disrupts vendor slot allocation and triggers liquidated damages clauses; AMOS does not automatically flag operational conflicts with maintenance slot windows

l4_steps.name: Monitor in-shop progress against TAT milestones
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (Work Order tracking)
l4_steps.input: Work package milestones, daily shop visit reports from vendor
l4_steps.output: Daily progress reports, milestone deviation flags in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Milestone adherence ≥90%; TAT variance ≤±10% of contracted schedule at mid-check review
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time visibility into vendor shop-floor status is absent in AMOS without a Resident Technical Representative on-site; no direct system-to-system integration between airline AMOS and most third-party MRO AMOS instances

l4_steps.name: Approve additional work findings (AWF) change orders
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + SAP Ariba (Change Order)
l4_steps.input: Vendor non-routine finding report, structural inspection results, AD/SB compliance requirement
l4_steps.output: Approved change order, updated work scope and cost estimate
l4_steps.kpi: AWF approval turnaround ≤4 hours to avoid vendor shop-floor downtime
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS change order approval workflow requires multiple sign-off tiers; delays in AWF approval are a leading cause of TAT overrun in heavy maintenance — vendors charge idle-time fees while awaiting airline decisions

l4_steps.name: Collect vendor scorecard data after work completion
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Tableau / Power BI
l4_steps.input: Completed work orders, TAT records, defect escapes, rework events, invoice data
l4_steps.output: Vendor performance scorecard with TAT, quality, and cost dimensions
l4_steps.kpi: On-time delivery ≥92%; rework rate ≤2%; defect escape rate (post-C-of-R finding) ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard data is manually aggregated from AMOS work orders and SAP cost postings; no automated vendor KPI dashboard — quarterly scorecard preparation takes 3–5 days of analyst effort

l4_steps.name: Conduct formal quarterly vendor performance review
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI (dashboards from AWS Redshift)
l4_steps.input: Vendor performance scorecard, SLA benchmarks, prior-quarter action items
l4_steps.output: Performance review minutes, corrective action plan if SLA threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: Quarterly performance reviews completed 100% on schedule; SLA compliance rating reported within ±5% confidence interval
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendors frequently dispute scorecard data citing their own internal metrics; absence of shared system-to-system data exchange creates reconciliation disputes that delay corrective action by 30–60 days

l4_steps.name: Issue corrective action request (CAR) for SLA breach
l4_steps.input: Failed performance review record, documented defect or delay pattern
l4_steps.output: Formal CAR with 30-day vendor response requirement, root cause analysis template
l4_steps.kpi: CAR vendor response rate 100% within 30 days; repeat findings reduced ≥50% within two subsequent work packages
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS Quality module CAR tracking provides no vendor portal access; all CAR follow-up is conducted via email outside the system, creating an unauditable correspondence trail for EASA Part-CAMO findings

l4_steps.name: Review and validate MRO vendor invoices (3-way match)
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) + AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice, completed AMOS work order, SAP Ariba PO, approved change orders
l4_steps.output: Invoice approval or dispute flag with line-item variance detail
l4_steps.kpi: 3-way match success rate ≥98%; invoice dispute resolution ≤15 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: 3-way match between AMOS work order, SAP Ariba PO, and vendor invoice frequently fails because AWF change orders are not captured in the original PO — each failure requires manual re-match across two systems

l4_steps.name: Process vendor payment and post maintenance cost allocation
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice, aircraft registration / cost centre mapping
l4_steps.output: Payment instruction, maintenance cost posted to aircraft-level cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Payment within contracted net-30 terms ≥95%; cost allocation accuracy 100% at aircraft registration level
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft cost centre mapping in SAP must align with AMOS aircraft registration codes; registration mismatches (e.g., wet-lease aircraft with swapped tails) cause fleet maintenance cost reporting errors that distort unit cost analysis

l4_steps.name: Evaluate contract renewal vs. re-tender decision
l4_steps.input: Aggregated vendor scorecard (12-month), market pricing benchmarks, contract expiry calendar
l4_steps.output: Renewal recommendation or re-tender decision brief for leadership sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal or re-tender decision completed ≥90 days before contract expiry; benchmark pricing variance ≤8% from renewed rate
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba does not proactively alert on contract expiry approaching 90-day threshold; contracts default to auto-rollover at existing rates, forfeiting leverage — market benchmark data requires manual sourcing from OAG or industry surveys

l4_steps.name: Execute contract close-out or new-vendor transition
l4_steps.role: Technical Services Manager + Procurement Specialist — MRO
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Renewal or re-tender decision, new vendor qualification record (if transitioning)
l4_steps.output: Closed-out contract record, active new vendor contract, knowledge transfer documentation
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor transition completed with zero AOG events attributable to transition gap; transition plan signed off ≥60 days before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Transitioning open AMOS work orders from outgoing to incoming vendor is a manual process with no system-supported migration wizard; open AWF items and warranty claims risk being orphaned during handover
